title: A field-friendly alternative to freeze-drying faeces for glucocorticoid metabolite analyses of African wild dogs (Lycaon pictus)
author: Postiglione, Accorsi, et al.

steps.title: Collect and freeze faecal samples
steps.instruction: Collect the entire dropping from known individual African wild dogs within 20 minutes of defecation; obtain 5 samples from Limpopo Lipadi Private Game and Wilderness Reserve (Botswana) and 5 samples from Khamab Nature Reserve (South Africa). Place each dropping into a sealable plastic bag, put the bag on ice immediately, and freeze the bag within two hours at –20 °C.

steps.title: Defrost and homogenize faeces
steps.instruction: Defrost each frozen sample and thoroughly mix the faecal material by hand over a cool surface.

steps.title: Divide samples into four aliquots
steps.instruction: For each individual, divide the mixed faeces into four equal subsamples that will be subjected to the four drying treatments.

steps.title: Dry aliquots using four methods
steps.instruction: Dry the subsamples as follows: (a) direct exposure to sunlight; (b) homemade solar oven (cardboard box lined with tin foil); (c) food dehydrator (Model K002, Mellerware, Johannesburg, South Africa) using a B22D 40 W halogen lamp and circulating fan; (d) freeze‑drying (Model ALPHA 1‑2 LD plus, Christ, Osterode, Germany).

substeps.instruction: Place each subsample in its assigned drying device.
Ensure the solar oven and dehydrator are set up according to the described models.

steps.title: Monitor drying progress and store dried samples
steps.instruction: Weigh each drying sample every four hours from 07:00 to 19:00; rotate the samples among positions every 4 h to equalize heat exposure; record temperature (sun 14‑43 °C, solar oven 14‑37 °C, dehydrator 29‑32 °C). Consider a sample dry when successive masses differ by less than 0.01 g. Once dry, reseal the bag and store the dried sample at room temperature (20‑25 °C) until assay.

steps.title: Pulverize and sieve dried faeces
steps.instruction: Pulverize the dried faeces and pass the material through a metal strainer to separate fine faecal powder from undigested debris.

steps.title: Extract hormones with ethanol
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.050–0.055 g of faecal powder, add 3 ml of 80 % ethanol in water, and vortex the mixture for 15 minutes to extract steroid metabolites.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the extract at 1 500 g for 10 minutes; transfer the resulting supernatant into sealed micro‑centrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Store extracts at -20 °C
steps.instruction: Keep the sealed micro‑centrifuge tubes containing supernatant at –20 °C until hormone analysis.

steps.title: Measure fGCM via competitive EIA
steps.instruction: Perform a competitive enzyme immunoassay using antibodies against cortisol‑3‑CMO:BSA and a cortisol‑3‑CMO‑DADOO‑biotin label. The assay sensitivity is 0.6 ng/g dry weight. Intra‑assay coefficients of variation are 5.67 % (high control) and 6.90 % (low control); inter‑assay coefficients of variation are 9.39 % (high) and 13.49 % (low). Follow the published protocol of the Endocrine Research Laboratory, University of Pretoria.
